sections.h2: Edmonson County Clerk hours and address
sections.html:
The Edmonson County Clerk works from 108 N. Main Street in Brownsville. The mailing address is P.O. Box 830, Brownsville, KY 42210, and the phone is 270-597-2624. Hours vary by day:

  • Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday: 8 in the morning until 4 in the afternoon
  • Thursday and Saturday: mornings only, closing at noon
  • Friday: 8 until 5

The Saturday morning hours help sellers who work weekdays. Brownsville holds the courthouse and is the one incorporated city in the county, so every deed for a house in Edmonson County, wherever it sits, comes to this one counter. Call before you go, since Thursday and Saturday close at noon and Friday stays open until 5.

sections.h2: How far back land records go
sections.html:
The clerk keeps most documents at the courthouse from 1840 to the present, and indexes reach back to 1840 for most document types. Images of nearly every instrument filed since January 1986 are online. All deeds from the county's start are online, and mortgage images are online from 1986 forward. Military discharge records are kept private for security reasons.

Online records include deeds, mortgages, mechanics liens, powers of attorney, wills, assignments, releases, tax liens and delinquent property taxes. That depth lets a seller or a title agent trace ownership of an old farm parcel without a trip to the courthouse.

The clerk posts a minimum fee table. A deed is $50, a mortgage is $80, and a full or partial release of mortgage is $46. Because these are minimums, confirm the total for a long document with the clerk before you go.

The clerk works with four e-recording services: Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Ask your closing agent whether they will submit the deed electronically instead of carrying paper to the counter. The office also offers an eCCLIX search.

Private citizens who live in the county can search Edmonson County records for personal reasons at no charge, limited to five searches a day. Commercial users pay a subscription. Anyone can view all public records in the clerk's office free of charge.

sections.h2: What is DOCALERT and why sign up?
sections.html:
DOCALERT is a free email service offered through the clerk's office. You register a name and an email address, and the service sends an alert whenever a mortgage or deed under that name is recorded in Edmonson County. The point is fraud protection: a filing you didn't sign would reach your inbox quickly.

Sellers who own several parcels, or who have inherited land held in a relative's name, may want to register every name tied to the property so a new filing doesn't go unseen.

The state taxes the grantor $0.50 per $500 slice of value, with any partial slice counted whole, and the clerk takes payment before recording. Value means the full consideration paid, including liens, or the fair market value for a gift or a deed with nominal consideration.

KRS 142.050 exempts foreclosure deeds, correction deeds, divorce transfers between spouses and nominal-value family deeds from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild. The clerk keeps 5 percent and forwards the balance to the county treasurer every three months.

sections.h2: When are tax bills due, and where do they go after April 15?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Office at 110 Jackson Street collects current bills. They are mailed on October 30, and anyone without one by November 15 should call 270-597-2157 for a duplicate. Payment through November 30 earns a 2 percent discount, December 1 to 31 is the base amount, January adds 5 percent and February 1 on adds 21 percent. Everything must be paid by April 15.

After that date the bill sits with the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency. The clerk advertises the delinquent real property bills in late summer and holds a sale at 11:00 a.m. at the courthouse. Bidders register shortly beforehand and must put down a 25 percent deposit. Taxpayers can pay the clerk in full any time before the sale, and payments received after the sale are returned.

The sheriff's collection calendar in short:

  • Bills mailed October 30
  • Through November 30: 2 percent discount
  • December 1 to 31: base amount
  • January: 5 percent added
  • From February 1: 21 percent added, with April 15 as the deadline

The Property Valuation Administrator at 110 E. Main Cross Street in Brownsville assesses all property in the county for the state, the county and other districts. Reach the office at 270-597-2381. Doors are open Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday from 7:30 until 4:30, and Thursday and Saturday mornings until noon.

Owners who disagree with a value must have a conference with the PVA during the May inspection period, then file with the clerk by the next workday after it closes. Residents past 65, or classified as totally disabled, can apply to the PVA for the $49,100 homestead exemption that applies for 2025 and 2026.

A city may adopt the county's annual assessment for property inside its limits, though vehicle taxes use a separate state-supervised assessment. In Edmonson County that point concerns Brownsville alone.

sections.h2: Other clerk services a seller may use
sections.html: The same counter serves drivers and voters. The clerk's site links to vehicle registration renewal, driver license renewal, voter registration, a lookup of vehicle tax paid last year by VIN, and bridge toll payments through River Link. Two links matter to a seller: Find and View Delinquent Taxes and Find and View Land Records, which opens the eCCLIX search.

Edmonson County covers 308 square miles in the Bowling Green metropolitan area, with Mammoth Cave National Park inside it. Population was 12,126 in 2020 and is estimated at 12,749 for July 2025, up 5.1 percent. There are 6,533 housing units, and 80.1 percent of households own. Homes typically value $160,300 and rent typically runs $778. One resident in five, 20.9 percent, is past 65, so the homestead exemption applies to many owners.

sections.h2: Getting a deed ready in Edmonson County
sections.html: Before you call the clerk, make a short list. Know the parcel and the names on your last recorded deed. Check online that any old mortgage release is on file. Decide whether your closing agent will e-record. Then phone 270-597-2624 for the total on a long document, and ask the sheriff for the current tax balance so it's cleared at closing. If you are selling an inherited parcel, bring the paperwork that shows how title passed, such as an affidavit of descent or a will, since those are recorded here too.

faqs.q: What is the Edmonson County Clerk's phone number?
faqs.a: 270-597-2624. The office is at 108 N. Main Street in Brownsville and is open Saturday mornings as well as weekdays.

faqs.q: What is the clerk's minimum fee for a deed in Edmonson County?
faqs.a: The minimum fee for a deed is $50. A deed of correction is $46, and a mortgage is $80.

faqs.q: Are Edmonson County deeds available online?
faqs.a: Yes. All deeds from the county's inception are online, and images of most instruments filed since January 1986 are online too. Mortgage images are online from 1986.

faqs.q: Can I pay a delinquent Edmonson County tax bill after the sheriff's deadline?
faqs.a: Yes, through the County Clerk. Pay in full before the advertised tax sale, since payments received after a sale are returned.

faqs.q: Does Edmonson County have more than one city?
faqs.a: No. Brownsville, the courthouse town, is the one municipality, so county offices handle nearly every tax question.
